partners.mechanism_chain: ABCC8 (HGNC:59) —DISRUPTS→ ATP-sensitive potassium channel (KATP) activity in pancreatic beta cells (GO:0005460); ATP-sensitive potassium channel (KATP) activity in pancreatic beta cells (GO:0005460) —LEADS_TO→ Hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia (HP:0011362); ATP-sensitive potassium channel (KATP) activity in pancreatic beta cells (GO:0005460) —LEADS_TO→ Neonatal diabetes mellitus (HP:0011357); Leucine (CHEBI:18089) —BINDS→ ATP-sensitive potassium channel (KATP) activity in pancreatic beta cells (GO:0005460). partners.mechanism_chain: INS (HGNC:5767) —DISRUPTS→ Insulin synthesis and secretion (GO:0007234); ABCC8 (HGNC:24) —DISRUPTS→ Insulin synthesis and secretion (GO:0007234); INS (HGNC:5767) —PRODUCES→ Proinsulin (CHEBI:17434); Proinsulin (CHEBI:17434) —DISRUPTS→ Insulin synthesis and secretion (GO:0007234); Insulin synthesis and secretion (GO:0007234) —LEADS_TO→ Hyperproinsulinemia (MONDO:0014535); Insulin synthesis and secretion (GO:0007234) —LEADS_TO→ Transient neonatal diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0012480). Mutations in either INS or ABCC8 impair the insulin synthesis and secretion pathway. #### 1. maturity-onset diabetes of the young, type 12  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.791)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-422356, Reactome:R-HSA-1296025, Reactome:R-HSA-5683177)

**Proposed mechanism:** ABCC8 pathogenic variant (null) —DISRUPTS→ ABCC8 (HGNC:59); ABCC8 (HGNC:59) —DISRUPTS→ KATP channel activity (GO:0005073); KATP channel activity (GO:0005073) —DECREASES→ Pancreatic beta-cell insulin secretion (REACT:R-HSA-70300); Pancreatic beta-cell insulin secretion (REACT:R-HSA-70300) —DECREASES→ Hyperglycemia (HP:0002119); Hyperglycemia (HP:0002119) —LEADS_TO→ Transient neonatal diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0012480); Hyperglycemia (HP:0002119) —LEADS_TO→ Maturity-onset diabetes of the young, type 12 (MONDO:0978299). Pathogenic variants in ABCC8 lead to loss of function of the KATP channel. This dysfunction impairs pancreatic beta-cell insulin secretion, resulting in hyperglycemia, which manifests as both transient neonatal diabetes mellitus type 2 and maturity-onset diabetes of the young type 12.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of ABCC8 variants with a gain-of-function effect in patients with either disease, or demonstration that ABCC8 mutations lead to distinct downstream molecular pathways for each disease. _(variant: null)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism of KATP channel dysfunction in ABCC8-related diabetes subtypes can inform therapeutic strategies targeting insulin secretion and glucose homeostasis.

#### 5. hypoglycemia, leucine-induced  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.717)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-422356, Reactome:R-HSA-1296025, Reactome:R-HSA-5683177)

**Proposed mechanism:** ABCC8 (HGNC:59) —DISRUPTS→ ATP-sensitive potassium channel (KATP) activity in pancreatic beta cells (GO:0005460); ATP-sensitive potassium channel (KATP) activity in pancreatic beta cells (GO:0005460) —LEADS_TO→ Hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia (HP:0011362); ATP-sensitive potassium channel (KATP) activity in pancreatic beta cells (GO:0005460) —LEADS_TO→ Neonatal diabetes mellitus (HP:0011357); Leucine (CHEBI:18089) —BINDS→ ATP-sensitive potassium channel (KATP) activity in pancreatic beta cells (GO:0005460). This leads to impaired glucose-stimulated insulin secretion in neonatal diabetes mellitus (Disease A). In leucine-induced hypoglycemia (Disease B), these same KATP channels are aberrantly sensitive to leucine, causing excessive insulin release even without elevated glucose, resulting in hypoglycemia.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of pathogenic variants in ABCC8 that are exclusively associated with one disease phenotype and not the other, or demonstration that the KATP channel function is differentially affected in a manner not explained by loss-of-function in both contexts. _(variant: The presence of common benign variants in ABCC8 in the gnomAD database that do not segregate with either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism involving ABCC8 and KATP channels opens avenues for targeted therapies. Mutations in either INS or ABCC8 impair the insulin synthesis and secretion pathway. Dysfunction of INS directly affects insulin processing, potentially leading to accumulation of proinsulin (hyperproinsulinemia). Mutations in ABCC8 disrupt the KATP channel function, which is essential for regulated insulin secretion, leading to both diabetes and potentially altered proinsulin processing and secretion dynamics.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in both ABCC8 and INS genes that are functionally distinct and do not converge on impaired insulin secretion or processing would falsify this hypothesis. **Why it matters:** Understanding this mechanistic link can inform therapeutic strategies for both transient neonatal diabetes and hyperproinsulinemia, potentially by targeting shared pathways in insulin production, processing, and secretion.
